exposure: Cervical dilation at diagnosis of the active phase of labor (4 vs 6 cm)
cohort: 3980 women with singleton, term pregnancy, and spontaneous labor in Malaysia between 2015 and 2019
finding: Active phase of labor at 6 cm cervical dilatation is associated with reduced primary caesarean delivery rate, labor intervention, shorter labor duration and fewer neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Active phase of labour at 6 cm cervical dilatation is associated with reduced primary caesarean delivery rate.
birth_weight: Lighter mean birth weight in the 6 cm group
